articles.titulo: The obesity-neuroinflammation-cancer axis: neuroimmune remodeling and therapeutic opportunities
articles.autores: Yang N, Zhang W, … Ding Z (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity is a chronic metabolic and inflammatory disorder associated with increased risk and poorer outcomes in multiple malignancies. Although adipose inflammation, insulin resistance, and altered adipokine signaling are established links between obesity and cancer, these mechanisms do not fully explain how systemic metabolic stress is translated into persistent changes in tissue immunity and tumor behavior. This narrative Review proposes the obesity-neuroinflammation-cancer axis as an integrative framework in which obesity-associated metabolic and inflammatory signals perturb central and peripheral neural homeostasis, while neuroinflammation, neural remodeling, and neuroendocrine signaling reshape the tumor microenvironment through reciprocal interactions among nerves, immune cells, stromal cells, and cancer cells. We focus on obesity-induced neuroinflammation, tumor neuroimmune remodeling, and neuroimmunometabolic feedback, highlighting sympathetic signaling, leptin-JAK/STAT3, NF-κB, inflammasome pathways, and metabolic reprogramming. We further evaluate therapeutic opportunities involving metabolic, inflammatory, and adrenergic interventions, including their combination with immune checkpoint blockade, while emphasizing inconsistent clinical evidence and the need for composite biomarkers. This framework is intended as a testable synthesis rather than a universally established causal pathway and identifies cancer-type-specific neuroimmune circuits as a priority for future translational research.

articles.titulo: Directional immuno-metabolic signatures following severe trauma are associated with organ-specific clinical endpoints in a prospective cohort
articles.autores: Osuchowski M, Fritsch G, … Zipperle J (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Severe trauma elicits evolving immune-metabolic responses that may differ across clinical endpoints. We characterized time-resolved innate and adaptive immune patterns associated with higher or lower endpoint odds during the first 96 h after injury.
Of 62 patients prospectively enrolled in the observational PRIME study (ISS >15), 52 met the prespecified analytical completeness criterion. Clinical and immune biomarkers were assessed at emergency room admission (ER), 24, 48, and 96 h. Time-point-specific quartile deviations were evaluated using logistic regression against microbiological culture positivity during hospitalization, creatinine-defined renal impairment, Berlin-defined ARDS of any severity, hepatic enzyme elevation, and four hemodynamic endpoints. Complementary sensitivity analyses and bootstrap resampling assessed the exploratory associations and their internal stability.
Microbiological culture positivity was associated with lower admission base excess and temperature, reduced CD4/CD8 ratios and CD4+ T-cell proportions at 24-48 h, and lower monocyte measures with higher IL-8 at 96 h. The 96-h monocyte CBC/IL-8 combination showed an apparent within-cohort AUC of 0.78. Creatinine-defined renal impairment was associated with lower admission pH and base excess and a higher-IL-8/lower-CD4/CD8 combination (apparent AUC 0.88), alongside later myeloid and lymphocyte-related alterations. Berlin-defined ARDS showed predominantly low-odds associations, including higher early pH and phagocytic capacity; its 96-h combination of lower phagocyte CD64 expression and lower lymphocyte percentage yielded an apparent AUC of 0.80. Hepatic enzyme elevation showed low-odds associations involving higher 96-h monocyte HLA-DR expression and lower CD64+ phagocyte counts (apparent AUC 0.78). Hemodynamic endpoints showed distinct, endpoint-specific high-odds configurations. Bootstrap selection reproducibility was limited for the retained multivariable combinations.
The evaluated clinical endpoints were associated with distinct directional immune-metabolic configurations rather than a uniform inflammatory response. Their hypothesis-generating contribution lies in the endpoint-specific organization of established biological components across serial sampling points. These exploratory candidate signatures require independent validation before their potential clinical relevance can be established.

articles.titulo: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy: Metabolic stress, inflammation, epigenetic reprogramming, and therapeutic strategies
articles.revista: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis
articles.autores: Samidurai A, Saravanan PB, … Kukreja RC (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a major form of non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy characterized by ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function following chronic alcohol exposure. Despite partial reversibility with prolonged abstinence, ACM remains an important cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, while the molecular mechanisms driving disease initiation and progression are incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that ACM is not solely a consequence of direct ethanol toxicity, but rather a complex disorder involving interconnected metabolic, inflammatory, immune, and epigenetic pathways. In this review, we summarize current advances in the pathophysiology of ACM and propose an integrated immunometabolic framework underlying disease progression. Chronic alcohol exposure induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium mishandling, and endoplasmic reticulum stress, leading to cardiomyocyte injury and impaired cellular energetics. These disturbances activate pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB and the NLRP3 inflammasome, promoting cytokine production and inflammatory forms of programmed cell death such as pyroptosis. Concurrently, accumulating evidence implicates immune dysregulation as a central contributor to adverse remodeling, characterized by altered T-cell polarization, macrophage phenotypic switching, and dysregulated immune checkpoint signaling that sustain chronic inflammation and fibrosis. In parallel, alcohol-induced epigenetic and post-transcriptional mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and microRNA-mediated regulation, establish persistent transcriptional reprogramming that links transient metabolic stress to long-term alterations in cardiomyocyte function and myocardial structure. Collectively, these pathways form a self-reinforcing network of metabolic injury, immune activation, and maladaptive remodeling that drives ACM progression. A more integrated understanding of these mechanisms identifies oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, immune imbalance, and epigenetic reprogramming as interconnected and potentially targetable processes. Therapeutic strategies combining alcohol abstinence with mechanism-based interventions targeting these pathways may provide new opportunities for precision treatment of ACM.

articles.titulo: Macrophage-state heterogeneity as the basis for host-directed therapy in tuberculosis
articles.autores: Shariq M, Ehtesham NZ, Hasnain SE (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tuberculosis (TB) persists partly because Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) occupies macrophages that differ in antimicrobial activity, nutrient use, inflammatory output, and drug exposure. This review examines how macrophage origin and lesion position influence phagosome maturation, responses to membrane damage, xenophagy, cytosolic sensing, regulated cell death, metabolism, and treatment response. Mtb can be taken up without lysosomal destruction, recognized by autophagy without completing lysosomal degradation, exposed to inflammatory signaling without effective killing, or retained in lesion regions with inadequate antibiotic concentrations. Evidence from single-cell studies, spatial analyses, experimental infection models, and clinical host-directed therapy studies supports evaluation of macrophage states rather than a fixed binary classification. Therapeutic candidates should be judged by linked host and bacterial outcomes, including completion of phagolysosomal or xenophagic degradation, viable bacterial burden, bacterial stress, preservation of macrophage and tissue function, lesion exposure, and compatibility with antimicrobial regimens. The evidence remains uneven: several mechanisms are well established, whereas many host-directed and nanomedicine approaches remain preclinical. Development should therefore use primary human macrophages, lesion-relevant models, lesion pharmacology, paired host-pathogen measurements, and separate microbiological, pathological, and functional endpoints. The aim is not broad immune stimulation but correction of defined macrophage and lesion states that permit persistence while preserving protective immunity.

articles.titulo: Ceramide-mediated immunometabolic modulation in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): emerging functions of sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 3 (SMPD3)
articles.autores: Mohammadi S, Darweesh M, … Al-Harrasi A (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a metabolically constrained and immunologically heterogeneous tumor microenvironment in which malignant, stromal, and immune cells compete for nutrients and exchange bioactive metabolites. Ceramide is a main sphingolipid intermediate and signaling lipid with several biological effects, which depend on acyl-chain composition, subcellular localization, metabolic flux, and cellular context. Sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 3 (SMPD3), also known as neutral sphingomyelinase 2 (nSMase2), generates ceramide through sphingomyelin hydrolysis and also participates in extracellular-vesicle biogenesis. HCC-specific findings claimed that reduced SMPD3 expression could be associated with adverse clinicopathological features and suppression of malignant phenotypes after SMPD3 restoration, could be in favor of a tumor-restraining function. However, direct evidence that endogenous SMPD3-derived ceramide reprograms the metabolism of infiltrating immune cells in primary HCC is currently lacking. This review distinguishes HCC-specific findings from mechanistic evidence derived from tumor and inflammatory systems. We integrate ceramide biosynthesis and turnover, HCC immunometabolism, T-cell and myeloid-cell metabolic states, extracellular-vesicle communication, and therapeutic studies using ceramide nanoliposomes. We also discuss the context-dependent relationship between ceramide and apoptosis, autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis, emphasizing that endogenous SMPD3-derived ceramide and exogenous short-chain ceramide formulations are not biologically interchangeable. Finally, we define experimental priorities required to test cell-specific SMPD3 functions, resolve ceramide species and spatial flux, validate biomarkers, and determine whether selective restoration of the SMPD3-ceramide axis can improve immunotherapy or other systemic treatment strategies in HCC.

articles.titulo: What do we really know about human immunometabolism in inflammatory disease?
articles.autores: Gunawardana S, Romero Arocha S, Clarke AJ (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cellular metabolism is now recognised as an active regulator of immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. However, much of this conceptual framework derives from in vitro systems and animal models that may not fully reproduce human physiology or disease. Many studies of human immune metabolism are constrained by artificial culture conditions, tissue dissociation, limited pathway coverage, and a reliance on static measurements that do not directly quantify metabolic flux in vivo. Interpretation is further complicated by the use of blood samples as a surrogate for diseases that arise in specialised tissues, such as synovium, gut, and skin, and by the influence of systemic physiology, including hepatic substrate regulation, adipose tissue, endocrine and neuronal signalling, and the gut microbiota. In this review, we examine what current experimental approaches can infer about immune metabolism in humans, with a focus on immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Oncology provides a valuable methodological precedent through its use of tissue sampling, spatial profiling, and stable isotope tracing, while also illustrating the challenges of assigning metabolic activity to individual cell populations within heterogeneous tissues. We propose five priorities for the field: move beyond blood to inflammatory tissue; complement static abundance with dynamic, stable isotope flux analysis; integrate single cell, spatial, and imaging modalities; incorporate carefully designed human metabolic perturbations; and account for the wider systemic and pre-analytical context. The next phase of human immunometabolism should move from pathway annotation in reductionist models towards dynamic, tissue-resolved, and clinically anchored studies of immune cell metabolism in vivo.

articles.titulo: Hepatocyte-derived lipid droplets in MASH: macrophage sensing and inflammation
articles.autores: Jin D, Zhao Y (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) develops through interactions between hepatocyte injury and hepatic immune responses. Lipid droplets (LDs) exposed or released from damaged hepatocytes provide a potential link between lipid accumulation and macrophage-mediated inflammation. Experimental studies indicate that these structures can both promote disease-associated macrophage responses and attenuate inflammatory signaling. This mini-review examines how hepatocyte-derived LDs influence macrophage sensing, uptake, and inflammatory responses in MASH. We discuss the contribution of membrane-spanning 4-domains A7 (MS4A7) to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and disease progression, alongside evidence that LD treatment suppresses inflammatory responses in cultured macrophages. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) supports this suppression without being required for LD uptake in the tested system, while reduced MS4A7 expression contributes to the attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings distinguish LD internalization from its downstream immune effects and warrant separate consideration from the efferocytosis of intact apoptotic hepatocytes. We examine experimental conditions and macrophage states as possible explanations for differing outcomes and identify unresolved questions about LD recognition and relevance to human disease. Finally, we consider therapeutic strategies that limit pathogenic macrophage activation while preserving beneficial clearance functions. Defining the molecular basis of LD sensing and establishing its consequences in vivo will be essential for translating this form of hepatocyte-macrophage communication into immunological interventions for MASH.

articles.titulo: Host immunometabolic reprogramming in paediatric refractory mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: cellular circuits, multi-omics signatures, and translational opportunities
articles.autores: Yang J, Cui S, … Liu J (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Paediatric refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which persistent microbial stimulation, dysregulated host immunity and evolving airway injury may coexist despite macrolide treatment. This review integrates clinical, experimental and multi-omics evidence to examine RMPP through an immunometabolic framework. Mycoplasma pneumoniae reprograms airway epithelial cells, macrophages and neutrophils by altering glycolysis, mitochondrial and redox signalling, autophagy and lipid and amino-acid metabolism. These responses can support early antimicrobial defence yet become maladaptive when inflammatory output is uncoupled from bacterial clearance. Epithelial ATP-dependent signalling, macrophage inflammasome activation, neutrophil aconitate decarboxylase 1 (ACOD1; historically termed immune-responsive gene 1 [IRG1])-itaconate activity and extracellular trap accumulation illustrate this context-dependent transition. Adaptive immune remodelling, compartment-specific Th17-regulatory T-cell imbalance and incomplete mucosal antibody protection may further sustain disease. Emerging metabolomic, lipidomic, microbiome and single-cell studies support biological heterogeneity but remain predominantly cross-sectional and cannot distinguish causal drivers from consequences of severe disease or treatment. Current mechanistic evidence is strongest for epithelial glycolysis and the neutrophil ACOD1-itaconate axis in experimental M. pneumoniae systems, whereas direct cell-resolved functional validation in paediatric RMPP remains limited, and ferroptosis and several proposed therapeutic targets remain provisional. We therefore present immunometabolic states as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than as validated endotypes. Future studies should determine whether dynamic combinations of pathogen burden, cell-specific metabolic function, inflammatory activity and anatomical injury reproducibly identify biological states that precede progression and predict differential treatment response. Longitudinal, cell-resolved studies integrating metabolic flux, pathogen trajectories, treatment exposure and anatomical evolution are required before these candidate states can support mechanism-informed clinical stratification.

articles.titulo: Metformin for the treatment of chronic liver disease: Mechanistic rationale, translational evidence, and repurposing opportunities
articles.autores: Vargas-Pozada EE, Ramos-Tovar E, … Muriel P (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is characterized by progressive hepatocellular injury, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, fibrogenesis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite advances in understanding CLD pathogenesis, effective therapies targeting multiple disease-driving pathways remain limited. Metformin, a biguanide widely used to treat type 2 diabetes, has emerged as a candidate for drug repurposing because of its pleiotropic metabolic and immunomodulatory effects. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale, translational evidence, and clinical implications of metformin in treating CLD. Experimental studies indicate that metformin modulates AMP-activated protein kinase-dependent and -independent pathways involved in hepatic lipid metabolism, mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative stress, autophagy, immunometabolic signaling, hepatic stellate cell activation, and hepatocarcinogenesis. In preclinical models, these effects have been associated with reduced steatosis, inflammatory injury, fibrogenesis, and tumor-promoting signaling. Epidemiological and clinical studies also suggest that metformin use is associated with improved survival in selected patients with cirrhosis and a lower risk of HCC in individuals with diabetes. Although mechanistic, experimental, and epidemiological evidence is encouraging, randomized clinical studies have not consistently shown histological improvement in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, and clinical findings remain heterogeneous across disease stages and etiologies. Limitations include the gap between mechanistic and clinical evidence, uncertainty regarding the relevance of proposed mechanisms, the context-dependent nature of metformin signaling, and the inherent limitations of observational studies. Overall, metformin is a biologically plausible therapeutic candidate for CLD, but its future clinical role will depend on integrating mechanistic insights with rigorous translational and clinical research to identify patients most likely to benefit.

articles.titulo: Time of day metabolism and endocrine regulation of immune health
articles.autores: Hattangady A, Singh V, … Kadambi V (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The immune system is a dynamic, energy-dependent network regulated by temporal biology. Advances in circadian biology have enabled the synchronizing of critical immune parameters such as metabolism, endocrine secretions, surveillance, tissue repair, and adaptation to environmental cycles. Here, we propose a metabolomic, and endocrine, chromodynamic model of immune health, based on time-of-day rhythms. Immune resilience is defined by synchronization among three groups of oscillators i) the central circadian clocks, ii) food-entrainable metabolic oscillators, iii) peripheral cellular clocks. The model provides a framework to optimize these interconnected systems to maintain metabolic efficiency, minimize unnecessary inflammation, and enable precise immune responses through temporal gating. External factors of modern lifestyle disruptions, including irregular feeding patterns, sleep deprivation, and chronic stress, induce internal circadian desynchrony, contributing to persistent low-grade inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, immune aging, and chronic non-communicable diseases. We propose that immune health is characterized not merely by the absence of disease, but by stable circadian phase coherence, low inflammatory noise, and adaptive immune resilience. We have listed some chrono-biomarkers of metabolomic and endocrine parameters that may provide a functional assessment of immune resilience, defined by inflammatory tone, immune adaptability, metabolic integrity, and repair capacity. This framework integrates chronobiology, endocrine and immunometabolism to shift medicine from reactive disease management toward proactive assessment and restoration of biological resilience.

articles.titulo: Brain insulin resistance and microglial immunometabolic dysregulation in neurodegenerative diseases
articles.autores: Liu X, Zhang X, … Zhang P (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Brain insulin resistance (BIR) is increasingly recognized as a contributor to the development and progression of neurodegenerative diseases rather than simply a metabolic abnormality. In the central nervous system, insulin signaling is involved in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, energy metabolism, and protein homeostasis. Increasing evidence suggests that impaired brain insulin signaling is associated with Alzheimer disease (AD), Parkinson disease (PD), and other neurodegenerative conditions, although the mechanisms linking BIR to persistent inflammation and neuronal injury remain incompletely understood. Microglia, the principal innate immune cells of the central nervous system, integrate metabolic and immune signals and may therefore provide an important link between impaired insulin signaling and chronic inflammation. BIR may disrupt insulin receptor substrate (IRS), phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), and protein kinase B (Akt) signaling and promote nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, impaired mitophagy, and lysosomal and lipid metabolic disturbances. These changes may promote activation of the NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, inflammatory mediator release, excessive phagocytosis, and synaptic dysfunction. In turn, persistent microglial inflammation may further impair insulin signaling, forming a reciprocal feedback loop that sustains pathological changes. This review summarizes the mechanisms linking BIR to microglial immunometabolic dysfunction and discusses potential therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic and inflammatory pathways in neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.titulo: Preoperative Opioid Use Predicts Socioeconomic Vulnerability and Worse Recovery in Elective Total Joint Arthroplasty
articles.autores: Barkus O, Zamzam M, … Charters M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Preoperative opioid prescription may be associated with postoperative outcomes after total joint arthroplasty (TJA). We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent primary TJA to assess associations between an active preoperative opioid prescription and 90-day complications, lengths of stay (LOS), discharge disposition, one-year patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), and socioeconomic vulnerability.
We identified 10,679 patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) or total knee arthroplasty (TKA) from 2018 to 2023. Preoperative opioid use was defined as an active opioid prescription within one month before surgery. This prescription-based definition served as a proxy for opioid exposure and did not confirm that prescriptions were filled or consumed. Outcomes included 90-day complications, LOS, discharge disposition, attainment of substantial clinical benefit (SCB) on PROMs collected from 2021 to 2023, and social vulnerability measured by the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Univariate analyses were used to identify candidate variables for multivariable logistic and negative binomial regression models.
Preoperative opioid prescription was identified in 3,935 patients (36.8%). Higher social vulnerability was independently associated with preoperative opioid prescription. In TKA, opioid prescription was independently associated with non-home discharge (odds ratio [OR] 2.07), pulmonary embolism (OR 3.47), longer length of stay (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.24), longer procedure duration (IRR 1.05), smaller improvements in the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (adjusted mean difference -2.44), and lower odds of SCB (OR 0.72). In THA, opioid prescription was independently associated with return to the operating room (OR 6.68), periprosthetic joint infection (OR 3.07), and longer postoperative stay (IRR 1.25).
Preoperative opioid prescription was common and was associated with worse outcomes in this TJA cohort. Patients who had a preoperative opioid prescription experienced longer LOS, more frequent non-home discharge, and reduced functional improvement after TKA. Opioid prescription was also correlated with greater socioeconomic vulnerability. Because no intervention was evaluated, these findings identify preoperative opioid prescription and socioeconomic vulnerability as markers of a higher-risk group rather than demonstrating that addressing either one reduces risk.

articles.titulo: Age-related shifts in dietary and oviposition preferences and steep costs of modest parental ageing in Drosophila melanogaster
articles.autores: Barker O, Ivimey-Cook ER, … Chapman T (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Nutritional requirements vary across sexes and lifetimes and are predicted to influence dietary preferences. Here, we tested the hypothesis that diet preferences vary adaptively with sex, age and life stage. We used the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster to take independent snapshots of choice for three protein : carbohydrate (P : C) diets in both sexes of young (5 d), mid-aged (15 d) or old (25 d) flies, while simultaneously recording oviposition site choice. We then tested, for mothers of each age, the diet preferences, development and survival on each diet of their larval offspring. Diet choice was sex- and age-specific. Males consistently preferred high carbohydrate, and females high protein (and these preferences became stronger with age). By contrast, oviposition choice was for balanced (1 : 1 P : C) and high carbohydrate diets in young and old females, respectively. Larvae of old, but not young, parents also preferred balanced diets. Young-parent larvae developed faster on balanced diets, with survival differences (highest with high carbohydrate) evident only in mid-aged-parent larvae. Unexpectedly, mid-aged-parent larvae had slower development and higher preadult mortality than young-parent larvae. Thus, diet choices may not be optimized across parents and offspring, and we identify novel effects of modest increases in parental age and offspring diets on offspring fitness.

articles.titulo: Health-Related Social Needs in a Large Health System: Comparing Mandated to Eight Additional Domains
articles.autores: Lockhart EA, Llamocca EN, … White-Perkins D (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
From 2024-2026, hospitals were mandated by Centers for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS) to screen for five health-related social needs (HRSN); however, patients experience additional HRSN that affect their health. Understanding all HRSN experienced among patients in large health systems is important to improve health.
To describe rates of patient-reported HRSN across 5 CMS-mandated, and 8 additional domains.
We conducted a cross-sectional study of all patient HRSN screenings completed in a large health system from July 2021 to June 2023. We summarized overall HRSN rates and utilized generalized estimating equation models to determine odds of experiencing HRSN across demographics.
Patients from a large, Midwestern healthcare system, aged ≥ 18 years and residing in the USA (n = 559,118).
Associations between patient demographics (sex assigned at birth, race, ethnicity, age, health insurance) and HRSN reported in 13 domains-five required by CMS (domestic violence; food, housing, and transportation insecurity; utility affordability) and eight additional domains (barriers due to physical/mental health; dependent care; employment; education; healthcare affordability; literacy; legal issues; social connections).
Four non-CMS-mandated categories had higher prevalence than any CMS-mandated category (barriers due to physical/mental health, 23.6%; education, 11.4%; social connections, 10.4%; literacy, 5.3%). Black patients and patients of Other race, patients aged 18-29 and 50-64 years old, and patients with Medicare/Medicare Supplement, Dual Medicaid + Medicare, Self-pay, and Other insurance had higher odds of reporting all CMS-required HRSN. Relative odds of other HRSN varied based on demographic characteristics.
This is one of the first studies to compare CMS-mandated HRSN and additional HRSN domains from a population-wide screening program. Future research should investigate what drives reported HRSN prevalence differences and ensure successful HRSN screening and intervention implementation across population subgroups. Determining which HRSN domains should be mandated by entities like CMS is paramount to addressing patient needs impacting health.

articles.titulo: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
articles.autores: Stark R, Patel P, … Dickman D (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca2+ (Cav2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high-release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low-release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Cav2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

articles.titulo: Loss of spermine synthase recapitulates RAS/MAPK and sensory processing phenotypes of Drosophila RASopathy models
articles.autores: van Reijmersdal B, de Wit M, … Schenck A (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hyperactivation of RAS/MAPK signaling is a hallmark of RASopathies, genetic developmental conditions associated with cognitive and sensory processing impairments. Genes linked to this pathway have been reported to be enriched among Drosophila models with habituation deficits, a behavioral phenotype reflecting impaired sensory filtering. To investigate whether RAS/MAPK overactivation extends beyond classical RASopathies, we generated 89 and screened 41 viable habituation deficient Drosophila RNAi models, measuring pathway activity as an increased phosphorylated ERK to ERK ratio. This screen identified Sms, the ortholog of human spermine synthase (SMS), implicated in Snyder-Robinson syndrome. RAS/MAPK overactivation along with hyperreactivity and habituation impairments were confirmed in a full loss-of-function mutant. An RNAi screen targeting polyamine pathway genes identified Sat (human SAT1/2, SATL1), with independent models reproducing aspects of these phenotypes. Knockdown of Sms or Sat in GABAergic neurons impaired habituation, suggesting a role for polyamine metabolism in inhibitory circuit function. These findings reveal previously unrecognized convergence between polyamine dysregulation and RASopathies, raising the possibility for shared therapeutic opportunities through modulation of either pathway.

articles.titulo: The Numb paradox: one protein, multiple isoforms, opposing functions in neurodevelopment, endocytic trafficking, and cancer
articles.autores: Gonzalez R, Reinberg D (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Numb is a multifunctional adaptor protein that serves as a central regulator of cell fate, linking polarity, signaling, and endocytic trafficking from early development to disease. Initially discovered in Drosophila melanogaster as an intrinsic determinant of asymmetric cell division, Numb's antagonism of Notch signaling has proven to be evolutionarily conserved in mammals, orchestrating the balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation during neurogenesis. In the mammalian brain, Numb and its paralog, Numb-like (Numbl), integrate polarity cues, receptor trafficking, and transcriptional networks to guide cortical development and maintain neural stem cell homeostasis. Alternative splicing generates multiple Numb isoforms (i.e., p72, p71, p66, and p65) that exhibit distinct structural and functional properties, allowing context-dependent modulation of Notch, p53, and integrin pathways. Isoform-specific expression patterns underlie divergent roles in neurodevelopment, neurite morphogenesis, and tumorigenesis, whereby Numb can act either as a tumor suppressor or as an oncogenic driver. Dysregulated splicing, posttranslational modification, and interaction with RNA-binding proteins such as RBM4, PTBP1, or SRSF9 reprogram Numb's activity across developmental and cancer contexts. Emerging evidence also connects Numb isoform regulation to neurodegenerative processes, including tauopathies and viral neuropathogenesis, as observed in Zika virus infection. Collectively, these findings position Numb as a molecular switch at the crossroads of neurodevelopment, cancer, and degeneration with its isoform diversity providing both mechanistic insight and therapeutic potential for restoring differentiation, restraining oncogenesis, and protecting neuronal integrity.

articles.titulo: Illuminating the Diversity of Electrical Synapse Form and Function
articles.autores: Bhattacharya A, Haas JS, … Martin EA (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: While the nervous system is organized by two main types of connections between neurons, electrical and chemical synapses, most studies focus upon the contribution of the molecularly complex and functionally diverse chemical synapse. Electrical synapses, in contrast, are perceived as simple, neuronal gap junction channels between contacts, often thought to be replaced in early development by more sophisticated chemical synapses. However, recent work and new tools push for the redefining of electrical synapse molecular architecture and function to allow for an updated interpretation of their ongoing contributions to neural circuit formation and function. Here, we describe fresh insight into neuronal gap junction structure, function, and molecular composition within invertebrate (nematodes, drosophila) and vertebrate (zebrafish, rabbit, rodent) model organisms across a variety of time periods and brain regions. Through molecular, genetic, connectomic, and functional explorations, our results argue for a new appreciation of electrical synapse heterogeneity. Based on these and other points of emerging new evidence, we argue for increased consideration of electrical synapses as complex and diverse structures which interact with chemical synapses to drive circuit formation and function.

articles.titulo: Structural Insights into Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers after Long-Term Operation Using Advanced 3D Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscopy Tomography
articles.autores: Poc JP, Park J, … Eichel RA (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are key to sustainable hydrogen production, but their long-term performance is limited by degradation, particularly in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which remains a barrier to commercial viability. Moreover, the need for corrosion-resistant materials and the intricate fabrication of bipolar plates and porous transport layers (PTLs) further impede large-scale deployment and account for a major share of the stack cost. Because lifetime and replacement costs are strongly influenced by the local microstructure and contact conditions, especially at the anode/PTL interface, a multiscale characterization approach combining 3D focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) with time-of-flight mass spectrometry is used to investigate degradation in an MEA after several thousand hours of operation under industrially relevant conditions. The 3D reconstruction and ppm-level chemical mapping show that local contact heterogeneities at welds in an expanded-metal mesh PTL act as degradation hotspots. At these sites, intensified catalyst utilization accelerates iridium dissolution, driving iridium migration and deposition as extended filaments into the membrane. Concurrently, membrane voids are formed beneath these sites, accompanied by iron contamination detected at both contact types. In contrast, general contact regions mainly show a thin redeposition layer without voids or filaments. These findings provide a mechanistic framework that links local contact conditions and microstructural heterogeneities to coupled catalyst and membrane degradation, supporting design rules for improved PEMWE durability.

articles.titulo: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
articles.autores: Vijayakumar P, Cauwenberghs K, … Su C-Y (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. Native tissues preserve extracellular particle organization and heterogeneity that are often lost during dissociation. Using cryofixation-based serial block-face scanning electron microscopy, we generated a nanoscale atlas of NVEPs and EVs across 352 Drosophila antennal olfactory sensilla ([~]70% coverage). Segmentation of more than 7,800 extracellular particles revealed distinct populations differing in morphology, size, electron density, and sensillum-class distribution. Analyses of EV biogenesis identified multivesicular bodies and membrane budding in auxiliary cells. Furthermore, sensilla housing degenerating neurons exhibited marked accumulation of EVs and NVEPs, accompanied by increased auxiliary-cell EV biogenesis. Together, these findings provide a large-scale ultrastructural characterization of extracellular particles in native sensory tissues and establish a foundation for understanding how extracellular particles are distributed, generated, and function during sensory signaling and degeneration.

Corpos multivesiculares e brotamento de membrana em células auxiliares apontam sítios de biogênese; sensilos com neurônios em degeneração têm mais vesículas e partículas.

articles.titulo: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase at the crossroads of redox homeostasis and regulated cell death in erythrocytes
articles.autores: Ulusu NN (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) provides the sole source of NADPH in mature erythrocytes, fueling the cell's essential antioxidant defenses. Although G6PD deficiency is traditionally tied to acute oxidative hemolysis, red cell loss extends beyond simple membrane rupture. This perspective evaluates G6PD-dependent NADPH supply as a metabolic redox checkpoint that controls the balance between erythrocyte survival, regulated cell death, and clearance. Reduced NADPH availability can limit glutathione regeneration and thus decrease GPX4-dependent lipid peroxide detoxification. Although this biochemical relationship provides a possible link between redox imbalance and erythrocyte injury, the direct involvement of ferroptosis and necroptosis-like pathways in mature erythrocytes remains insufficiently proven. Acute hemolysis, in this view, is a downstream consequence of these regulated events rather than the primary cause. G6PD is essential for erythrocyte survival as their sole source of NADPH. G6PD deficiency alone does not always cause cell death, but under oxidative stress, it acts as a metabolic checkpoint that shifts red blood cells from survival to regulated death rather than simple osmotic lysis.

articles.titulo: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination
articles.autores: Tchouatieu AM, Wells TNC, Achan J (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

articles.titulo: Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90 supports DNA replication
articles.autores: Ibrasheva G, Chen Y, … Derbyshire ER (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Plasmodium falciparum heat shock protein 90 (PfHsp90) is an attractive antimalarial target, but the molecular pathways dependent on its activity remain poorly understood. Here, we use two chemically distinct Hsp90 inhibitors, geldanamycin and XL888, to profile the PfHsp90-dependent proteome during the blood stage. We identify 131 proteins reduced in abundance following both treatments, 40% of which co-immunoprecipitate with PfHsp90. DNA replication emerges as the most enriched pathway, and PfHsp90 inhibition reduces parasite DNA content and nascent DNA synthesis during blood- and liver-stage development. Combining Hsp90 inhibition with inhibitors of DNA replication further produces synergistic antiparasitic activity. Together, these findings establish a functional connection between PfHsp90 and parasite DNA replication and define a network of conserved and Plasmodium-specific proteins dependent on Hsp90 activity.

A inibição reduz o conteúdo de DNA e a síntese de DNA nascente nos estágios sanguíneo e hepático e é sinérgica com inibidores de replicação.

articles.titulo: Impact of pfhrp2/pfhrp3 Gene Deletions on the Diagnostic Performance of HRP2-Based Rapid Diagnostic Tests for Plasmodium falciparum in sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
articles.autores: Nwinyi OC, Justus AC (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Histidine-rich protein 2 (HRP2)-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are widely used for the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in sub-Saharan Africa. However, deletions of the pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 genes threaten the accuracy of these tests by causing false-negative results. This study systematically reviewed and synthesized available evidence on the prevalence of pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 gene deletions and their implications for HRP2-based RDT performance in sub-Saharan Africa. A systematic review and meta-analysis were registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261443503) and were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Four electronic databases were searched for studies published between January 2015 and June 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled prevalence, while heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, τ², and I² statistics. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 gene deletions was 3.64% (95% CI: 1.86%-7.01%), 1.63% (95% CI: 0.54%-4.79%), and 1.94% (95% CI: 0.90%-4.14%), respectively. High between-study heterogeneity was observed across all analyses (I² > 91%), reflecting considerable geographical and methodological variability. Diagnostic accuracy analysis demonstrated that HRP2-based RDTs maintained high overall sensitivity and specificity but exhibited reduced sensitivity in settings where pfhrp2 and/or pfhrp3 deletions were prevalent, resulting in false-negative diagnoses and compromised detection of P. falciparum infections. While most studies reported low deletion frequencies, localized hotspots with substantially higher prevalence highlighted areas at greater risk of diagnostic failure. pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual gene deletions remain relatively uncommon across sub-Saharan Africa but exhibit marked geographical variation. Their presence can reduce the diagnostic performance of HRP2-based RDTs, underscoring the need for continuous molecular surveillance, routine monitoring of RDT performance, and the adoption of complementary diagnostic strategies in areas with increasing deletion prevalence.

articles.titulo: Development of a climate-sensitive disease forecasting tool in the Horn of Africa: A multi-stakeholder exploration of priorities in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda
articles.autores: Cornell TR, Kankya C, … Fèvre EM (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Extreme climate events impose significant impacts across the Horn of Africa. One way to monitor these is by using novel digital tools to forecast extreme events and climate-sensitive disease outbreaks. However, limited information exists on stakeholder use of such tools. This qualitative study identified key multidisciplinary stakeholders in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda, and conducted a needs assessment and gap analysis. Focal persons of multi-lateral agencies, government institutions and ministries, non-governmental organisations, and academic institutions, at regional, national, and sub-national levels, were engaged in Key Informant Interviews (KIIs; N = 63) and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs; N = 7, total participants = 57). Malaria (54.0%), Rift Valley Fever (RVF; 44.4%), cholera (39.7%), dengue fever (27.0%), and anthrax (14.3%) were the most frequently reported climate-sensitive disease priorities amongst KII participants. Country-level variations existed in the use of climate or environmental data to support disease decision-making (Kenya: 95.2% of KII participants, Uganda: 75.0%, Somalia: 64.3%, Ethiopia: 58.3%), electronic reporting systems (Kenya: 42.9%, Ethiopia: 41.7%, Somalia: 14.3%, Uganda: 12.5%), and modelled outputs (Kenya: 57.1%, Uganda: 25.0%, Somalia: 7.1%). FGD participants described barriers to sustainable digitalised systems including cost-effectiveness, lack of technological expertise or support, and poor Internet access, which may be addressed by engaging key national stakeholders, training provision, and financial resources. Overall, digital tool preferences for analysing, displaying or reporting data included provision of data summaries and visual aids, a dashboard format, and functions to download data for further analysis. This study provides critical insights into the needs of disease control stakeholders who would benefit from, and are the likely primary users of, digital tools to tackle the increasing threat of climate-sensitive diseases. It underscores the importance of applying context-specific approaches to supporting local capacity, which will inform the development of a sustainable Climate Sensitive Disease Forecasting Tool (CLIMSEDIS).

articles.titulo: Seasonal variation of immature mosquitoes in rice fields and their association with water quality and crop growth stages in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam
articles.autores: Duong CV, Ngo QKT, Nguyen VV (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rice agroecosystems are among the most productive mosquito habitats in Asia, but the ways in which crop phenology and urbanisation-driven environmental changes shape immature mosquito vector populations remain poorly understood. We quantified mosquito larvae and pupae dynamics across two crop seasons in a rice field located in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam, using generalised linear models with appropriate error distributions. A total of 3196 immature mosquitoes representing six species were collected. Overall mosquito abundance was significantly higher in spring than in autumn and peaked during the vegetative stage. Species richness did not vary between seasons but declined significantly at later crop stages. Larval-stage structure varied with both season and crop phenology. Early instars were more prevalent in spring and during the reproductive stage, whereas late instars dominated in autumn and declined during the ripening stage. The proportion of pupae decreased during the reproductive stage. Among dominant taxa, Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Anopheles barbirostris showed strong seasonal responses, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus exhibited no significant temporal variation. Environmental drivers differed among species. Culex tritaeniorhynchus was positively associated with water depth, pH and dissolved oxygen, but negatively associated with conductivity. In contrast, Cx. quinquefasciatus was strongly associated with higher conductivity, while An. barbirostris showed negative associations with temperature and conductivity. These findings indicate that mosquito development in rice fields is jointly structured by crop seasonality and agronomic water management, with early crop stages creating favourable conditions for larval proliferation. The dominance of vector species of epidemiological concern underscores the need to integrate phenology-based habitat management into nuisance and mosquito vector control strategies in Hanoi and similar peri-urban rice-growing landscapes.

v6.resumo: Em arrozal periurbano de Hanói, 3.196 imaturos de seis espécies em duas safras; abundância maior na primavera e no estágio vegetativo; Cx. tritaeniorhynchus associado a profundidade, pH e oxigênio dissolvido, Cx. quinquefasciatus a condutividade e An. barbirostris negativamente a temperatura e condutividade.
v6.metodo: Coletas de larvas e pupas, modelos lineares generalizados.

articles.titulo: Risk indicators and composite index for imported malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China: a 10-year study integrating case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data
articles.autores: Liao Q, Wang J, … Wu Z (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Following China's malaria-free certification in 2021, imported malaria infections and the continued presence of Anopheles mosquitoes pose challenges for preventing local transmission in post-elimination settings. We integrated case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data to describe potential conditions for malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China.
We analyzed imported malaria cases reported during 2016-2025, vector surveillance records, and corresponding meteorological data. Five binary indicators-imported case presence, diagnostic delay, Anopheles presence, high Anopheles density, and favorable meteorological conditions-were combined into an exploratory monthly index. Risk scores were tabulated for the 60 months in the May-October surveillance seasons using the available routine surveillance information.
A total of 663 imported malaria cases were reported, of which 611 (92.2%) originated from Africa. In the 37 months with matched vector and meteorological records, concurrent precipitation was positively associated with Anopheles density (Spearman's ρ = 0.360, P = 0.031), whereas mean temperature and dew point temperature 2 months earlier were negatively associated with density (ρ = - 0.504, P = 0.002; and ρ = - 0.578, P < 0.001, respectively). Of the 60 seasonal months, 28 (46.7%) were assigned low-risk scores, 27 (45.0%) moderate-risk scores, and 5 (8.3%) high-risk scores. All five high-risk months occurred in May or June.
The exploratory index identified seasonal variation in the concurrence of routinely monitored indicators, with high-risk scores observed in May and June. Year-round case surveillance and timely diagnosis remain important, alongside vector monitoring during the surveillance season. Uneven monitoring coverage and the lack of validation against local transmission events limit interpretation of the resulting risk categories.

Em 37 meses pareados, a densidade de Anopheles correlacionou com precipitação (ρ=0,360) e negativamente com temperatura dois meses antes (ρ=−0,504); o índice não foi validado contra transmissão local.
v6.metodo: Correlação de Spearman entre densidade vetorial e variáveis meteorológicas; escore mensal por soma de indicadores binários.

articles.titulo: Spatio-temporal clustering of dengue in Valle del Cauca, Colombia
articles.autores: Sy H, Vargas-Gonzalez DA, … Alexander ND (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue is endemic in Colombia's Valle del Cauca region. The precise timing and spatial scale of seasonal dengue transmission necessary for effective reactive interventions at the sub-municipal level across the 42 municipalities of Valle del Cauca remain unclear. This study aimed to identify spatio-temporal dengue clusters in Valle del Cauca.
A retrospective observational study was conducted using individual laboratory-confirmed dengue cases, including residential geolocation and consultation dates, reported by healthcare providers to the Sistema Nacional de Vigilancia en Salud Pública (SIVIGILA) in 2022. Residence was utilized as the probable site of infection. Spatio-temporal clustering was analyzed using Kulldorff's space-time scan statistic to identify statistically significant dengue clusters. Results were mapped using R. As a second aim, the association between clinical and demographic characteristics and dengue hospitalization was evaluated. Of 3,964 dengue cases reported in Valle del Cauca in 2022, 2,232 (56%) were laboratory-confirmed. Of these, 1,973 occurred in the defined areas of the nine municipalities included in the spatio-temporal analysis of this study. We identified 28 clusters at the sub-municipal level, with radii of 0-0.98 km, lasting 1-6 months and containing 10-114 cases. Twenty-six clusters (92.9%) spanned both warm-dry and cool-wet seasons, and clusters accounted for 32.0% of spatially analyzed cases. 960 patients were hospitalized. Lower socioeconomic status (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.57), enrollment in the state-subsidized insurance scheme (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.41-2.15) compared with the contributory scheme, and age ≥ 70 years compared to ages 20-29 years (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.51-4.04) were associated with higher odds of hospitalization.
This study identified dengue clusters at the sub-municipal level with the potential to inform reactive dengue control interventions and demonstrated a disproportionate impact on socioeconomically disadvantaged populations and the elderly in Valle del Cauca, Colombia.

v6.implicacao: Escala dos clusters (menos de 1 km, meses) como referência para os seis recortes de Aedes no Rio (Epidemiologia de Precisão, cooperação com a SVS).
v6.resumo: Varredura espaço-temporal de Kulldorff em 1.973 casos de dengue confirmados (SIVIGILA, 2022) em nove municípios do Valle del Cauca: 28 clusters sub-municipais, raio de 0 a 0,98 km, duração de 1 a 6 meses; hospitalização associada a menor nível socioeconômico, regime subsidiado e idade a partir de 70 anos.
v6.metodo: Estatística de varredura espaço-temporal com residência como local provável de infecção, mapas em R, regressão para hospitalização.

articles.titulo: Generation and Validation of a Panel of Epitope-Tagged UAS-Ubiquitin Transgenes for Tissue-specific Analysis of Ubiquitination in Drosophila
articles.autores: Kala-Bhattacharjee S, Davis S, … Wu C (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ubiquitination is a highly regulated post-translational modification that controls protein stability, activity, localization, and interactions, and its disruption process contributes to a broad range of human diseases, including cancer, neurodegeneration, and immune dysfunction. The genetic model organism Drosophila melanogaster offers powerful in vivo tools for studying ubiquitination, including the GAL4/UAS, Split-GAL4, GeneSwitch, and MARCM system, which can be combined with imaging and biochemical approaches to achieve precise spatial and temporal analyses. Realizing this potential, however, requires epitope-tagged UAS-Ubiquitin transgenes-both unmodified and chain-restricted-that behave like endogenous ubiquitin. Here we report a screen to generate and validate such a panel. We first defined the endogenous ubiquitination pattern at larval neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) as a bench mark, then compared it with a series of transgenically expressed, tagged ubiquitin in muscle and neurons. His-Myc-, HA-, and His-Biotin-tagged ubiquitins reproduced endogenous postsynaptic ubiquitination pattern and, by anti-tag immunoprecipitation followed by anti-ubiquitin immunoblotting, were shown to be covalently incorporated into ubiquitin conjugates in vivo. In contrast, a larger NTAP-tagged ubiquitin failed to conjugate at the postsynaptic density. Expression of the validated transgenes did not alter NMJ bouton number. We describe the practical uses of the validated transgenes for tissue-specific imaging and affinity purification, together with their limitations, to help investigators select appropriate tools for studying ubiquitination across diverse cellular and developmental contexts.

articles.titulo: Comparative analysis of serum antibody responses and immune landscapes in patients with acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and Chikungunya virus infections
articles.autores: Zhang Y, Zhang S, … Wu N (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are major mosquito-borne arboviruses that increasingly co-circulate in tropical and subtropical regions, including southern China. However, the extent to which these viruses induce shared or distinct host immune responses remains poorly understood. This study aimed to comparatively characterize immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections.
A total of 80 serum samples were analyzed, including 65 samples from patients with laboratory-confirmed DENV-1 (n = 29), DENV-2 (n = 10), or CHIKV (n = 26) infections and 15 healthy controls.Viral RNA was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction. Virus-specific IgM and IgG responses were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and serum cytokines were quantified using a multiplex assay. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests, and associations among antibody responses, cytokine concentrations, and viral RNA levels were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure.
The three infections shared features of interferon-associated immune activation and relatively restrained systemic inflammation but exhibited distinct immune mediator profiles, characterized by differential inflammatory mediator and growth factor responses. After multiple-testing correction, cytokine-cytokine correlation analysis revealed both shared and infection-specific patterns of immune mediator covariation, with shared associations involving IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4, and CXCL1 across all three infection groups. Positive associations between pathogen-specific IgM responses and Ct values were observed across the infections, although the association was not statistically significant for DENV-2 after multiple-testing correction. IgG responses showed a similar association only in DENV-1 infection. Integration of cytokine and antibody profiles further revealed distinct immune association patterns: DENV-1 showed broader associations involving viral RNA levels, inflammatory mediators, and humoral responses, whereas CHIKV displayed a more restricted pattern centered on associations between inflammatory mediators and IgM responses.
These findings reveal shared and distinct immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections and provide a comparative framework for investigating virus-associated immune regulation during acute arboviral infections.

v6.resumo: 80 soros (DENV-1 n=29, DENV-2 n=10, CHIKV n=26, controles n=15): ativação associada a interferon e inflamação sistêmica contida nos três grupos, com perfis de mediadores distintos; associações compartilhadas envolvendo IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4 e CXCL1 após correção de Benjamini-Hochberg.

articles.titulo: Impact of partial oxygen pressure on Zika-VLP production using Sf-9 rhabdovirus negative (Sf-RVN®) insect cell line
articles.autores: Aragão Tejo Dias V, Jorge Atanes Netto R, … Fernández Núñez EG (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) causes congenital and neurological complications, but no approved vaccine or therapy is available. Virus-like particles (VLP) are a promising vaccine platform, and dissolved oxygen is a critical parameter in insect cell bioprocesses. This study evaluated how partial oxygen pressure (pO2) affects ZIKV-VLP production in the rhabdovirus-negative Spodoptera frugiperda Sf-RVN® cell line, grown in chemically defined medium and infected with a recombinant baculovirus encoding capsid, membrane precursor, and envelope proteins. Cells were cultivated at 30%, 20%, and 10% air saturation pO2, and growth, cell death, oxygen uptake, baculovirus production, and envelope protein expression were analyzed. Sf-RVN® cells produced ZIKV-VLP under all conditions, with physiological behavior comparable to Sf-9 cells. Among the pO2 conditions evaluated, 30% pO2 yielded the highest specific envelope protein production rate (22.5 pg 106 cells-1 h-1) and volumetric productivity (32.2 pg mL-1 h-1). The VLP showed sizes and structural features consistent with previous reports. These results support Sf-RVN® cells as a safe and consistent platform for ZIKV-VLP production.

articles.titulo: Maternal-fetal health in arboviral diseases: clinical outcomes following prenatal dengue and chikungunya virus infections
articles.autores: Salem GM, Tang KH, … Foo S-S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: SUMMARYArthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) are an increasingly important cause of global infectious disease, yet their effects during pregnancy and early life remain incompletely understood. In the context of declining fertility and birth rates globally, infectious threats to successful pregnancy and neonatal health warrant greater attention. Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), two of the most prevalent mosquito-borne viruses, are underrecognized contributors to maternal-fetal health. Although these infections rarely result in classical congenital syndromes, accumulating clinical, epidemiological, and experimental evidence indicates that prenatal exposure can impair placental function, drive maternal immune dysregulation, and influence fetal and neonatal immune development. This review summarizes current knowledge on the maternal, placental, and pediatric consequences of DENV and CHIKV infection during pregnancy. We outline the immunological features of the maternal-fetal interface and discuss how pregnancy-associated immune modulation shapes antiviral responses and placental homeostasis. We then review epidemiological and clinical evidence linking prenatal arboviral infection with adverse pregnancy outcomes, neonatal disease, and potential long-term neurodevelopmental effects. Mechanistic insights, including viral immune evasion, placental inflammation, and antibody-mediated immunopathology, are examined. Finally, we discuss clinical considerations for monitoring arboviral-exposed pregnancies and progenies, alongside emerging strategies to reduce maternal infection and improve neonatal outcomes.

v6.resumo: Revisão (Clin Microbiol Rev) sobre DENV e CHIKV na gravidez: disfunção placentária, desregulação imune materna e efeitos sobre o desenvolvimento imune fetal e neonatal; discute evasão imune viral, inflamação placentária e imunopatologia mediada por anticorpos, e o acompanhamento de gestações expostas.
