articles.titulo: A bispecific mRNA vaccine against zika and dengue viruses to overcome antibody-dependent enhancement and provide protection in preclinical models
articles.autores: Shi H, Xie D, … Huang Y (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) are two widespread flaviviruses that pose a significant threat to public health. Owing to their extensive co-circulation and antigenic cross-reactivity, both viruses carry the risk of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), a phenomenon that renders existing vaccines unable to simultaneously protect against both pathogens. To overcome this limitation, we developed a bispecific mRNA vaccine against ZIKV and DENV (bis-mZDV) by integrating orthogonal B-cell and T-cell modules. The B-cell module was constructed by fusing ZIKV EDIII to the self-adjuvanting complement component C3d to enhance neutralizing antibody titers. The T-cell module incorporated conserved epitopes from ZIKV and DENV, thereby inducing cross-reactive CD8⁺ T cells without eliciting ADE-prone B-cell responses. Notably, the new bis-mZDV achieved up to an 8-fold enhancement in neutralizing antibody titers compared to the unadjuvanted EDIII mRNA vaccine. More importantly, in immunodeficient mice, it conferred protection against both ZIKV and DENV challenges and elicited robust humoral and cellular immune responses. The bis-mZDV represents a promising strategy that may be applicable to co-circulating pathogens and other viruses associated with ADE.

articles.titulo: Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro and chikungunya viruses as causative agents of febrile syndrome in Colombian patients during 2013 and 2014
articles.autores: Rodas JD, Montoya-Ruíz C, … Weaver SC (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Colombia's tropical climate and low-altitude cities create an ideal environment where mosquito-borne diseases can thrive. During 2013-2014, dengue was the most diagnosed cause of febrile syndrome. However, other viruses like Venezuelan equine encephalitis (VEEV), Mayaro (MAYV), and chikungunya viruses (CHIKV) were also present, and their true prevalence was likely underestimated due to limited surveillance.
We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 90 febrile malaria- and dengue-negative patients from the Urabá region. For each patient, we collected both acute and convalescent serum samples, which were analyzed to detect antibodies against VEEV, CHIKV, and MAYV. Additionally, we attempted virus isolation from the acute-phase serum samples.
We found that antibodies against VEEV were present in 28.3% of samples, CHIKV antibodies were detected in 5%, and MAYV antibodies in 1.7%. Notably, one patient seroconverted against CHIKV even before the first outbreak was recognized in Colombia in 2014. Furthermore, we isolated and fully sequenced VEEV, and our analysis revealed a close phylogenetic relationship with subtype ID Panamanian strains.
This study highlights the need to consider arboviruses beyond just dengue (DENV), when evaluating febrile illness in Colombia. The detection of VEEV and CHIKV, even before they were officially recognized as significant public health threats in this region, underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

v6.resumo: Em 90 pacientes febris negativos para malária e dengue em Urabá, Colômbia (2013–2014), anticorpos contra VEEV em 28,3%, CHIKV em 5% e MAYV em 1,7%; um paciente soroconverteu para CHIKV antes do primeiro surto reconhecido; VEEV isolado e sequenciado, próximo ao subtipo ID panamenho.
v6.metodo: Soros agudo e convalescente, sorologia, isolamento viral e sequenciamento.

articles.titulo: Defining the druggability of viral macrodomains in coronaviruses and alphaviruses
articles.autores: Biswas B, Abraham R, … Leung AKL (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Viral macrodomains are ADP-ribosylhydrolases encoded within the nonstructural proteins of coronaviruses and alphaviruses-2 RNA virus families with pandemic potential. Genetic studies demonstrate that ADP-ribose binding and ADP-ribosylhydrolase activity are critical for replication in alphaviruses and select coronaviruses, such as Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus and murine hepatitis virus. In contrast, for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and SARS-CoV-2, this domain primarily enhances in vivo fitness by modulating the innate immune response, establishing the macrodomain as a validated antiviral target. Structure-guided and high-throughput efforts have identified selective inhibitors for SARS-CoV-2 and, more recently, early-stage inhibitors of the alphavirus chikungunya virus. Both exploit a conserved active-site architecture that organizes ligand recognition into adenine, phosphate, ribose, and oxyanion subsites. Despite screening of extensive chemical libraries, inhibitor discovery has repeatedly converged on adenine-anchored scaffolds requiring polar engagement of the oxyanion region to achieve potency. This convergence defines a structurally confined druggable corridor but reveals a persistent permeability-potency tradeoff imposed by the polarity required for catalytic engagement. Cross-family comparisons further demonstrate localized divergence that shapes selectivity and constrains straightforward scaffold portability. Here, we synthesize structural, biochemical, and antiviral advances across SARS-CoV-2 and chikungunya virus, define the current boundaries of macrodomain chemical space, and delineate the chemical and biological constraints that now govern translation of catalytic inhibition into predictable antiviral efficacy. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Viral macrodomains have emerged as compelling antiviral targets in 2 pandemic-potential virus families, coronaviruses and alphaviruses, owing to their conservation and role in virulence. This review defines the chemical space and druggability of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and chikungunya virus macrodomains and the structural and biological constraints that must be overcome to translate catalytic inhibition into next-generation antivirals.

articles.titulo: Heterogeneous Permissiveness of Chicken Cells and Tissues to Oropouche Viruses
articles.autores: Limonta D, Salas-Quinchucua C, … Osorio JE (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Massive outbreaks of a reassortant Oropouche virus (OROV) spread across Latin America and the Caribbean in 2023-2025. OROV is a reemerging arbovirus belonging to the trisegmented RNA peribunyavirus family. Viral transmission occurs in sylvatic and urban cycles involving humans and other vertebrates with Culicoides biting midges as the main vector in urban settings. Anti-OROV antibodies have been found in domestic and wild birds in Brazilian OROV-endemic areas. However, no studies exist on the permissiveness of OROV in avian models, and the contribution of birds to the OROV spread remains largely unexplored. Our research indicates that chicken embryonic fibroblasts and chicken tissue explants from the liver, heart, and lung are selectively infected by OROV strains isolated by our group in South America, including the novel OROV reassortant. This work contributes to the development of avian models to investigate new determinants in the infection and transmission of an important arbovirus in the Americas.

v6.resumo: Fibroblastos embrionários e explantes de fígado, coração e pulmão de galinha são infectados por cepas de OROV da América do Sul, incluindo o novo rearranjo; propõe modelo aviário para determinantes de infecção e transmissão.
v6.metodo: Infecção de células e explantes de tecido de galinha com isolados de OROV.

articles.titulo: Filamentous cyanobacterial blooms (Pseudanabaena and Cylindrospermopsis) result in the simplification of functional genes involved in nitrogen and phosphorus cycles
articles.autores: Qiu P, Li C, … Bi Y (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) threaten freshwater ecosystems and are linked to nutrient cycling. We conducted a metagenomic investigation in China's Yuqiao Reservoir, which experiences filamentous cyanobacterial blooms (Pseudanabaena and Cylindrospermopsis), to elucidate microbial mechanisms driving nitrogen and phosphorus cycling during HABs. 28 genes for both nitrogen-cycling and phosphorus-cycling showed significantly different abundances between bloom and non-bloom periods. Bloom periods exhibited unified, energy-efficient metabolic strategies, featuring upregulated genes for nitrogen uptake via ammonia assimilation (gltB/D) and enhanced inorganic phosphorus uptake, including high-affinity phosphate transporters (pstA/B/C) and polyphosphate storage genes (ppk1, phoU), supporting rapid microbial proliferation. Conversely, non-bloom periods showed a metabolic transition to diversified nitrogen acquisition, including upregulation of nitrate assimilation, nitrification, denitrification, coupled nitrification-denitrification, and nitrogen fixation. Organic phosphorus mineralization genes became predominant. Concurrently, significant restructuring occurred in both nitrogen- and phosphorus-cycling communities. Although composed predominantly of Actinobacteria, Cyanobacteria, and Proteobacteria in both periods, keystone taxon analysis revealed a critical functional shift from an "autotrophic cyanobacteria-driven" pattern during blooms to a "heterotrophic bacteria-mediated metabolism" in non-bloom phases. Microbial co-occurrence network analysis indicated that the algal bloom triggered a fundamental community reorganization, from a broadly cooperative and stable structure to a more partitioned and potentially specialized state, reflecting strong niche partitioning due to altered environmental conditions. Partial least squares path modeling confirmed that algal blooms govern functional gene abundance by driving microbial community restructuring. Our findings demonstrate that microbial metabolic pattern mediated by algal blooms determined the unification of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling genes, revealing the mechanisms of HABs' ecological impacts.

articles.titulo: Siamese banana peel-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles and their broad-spectrum antibacterial activity
articles.autores: Van Nguyen TT, Nguyen PA, … Nguyen T (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Plant-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using agricultural by-products is not only a strategy to develop sustainable nanoparticle synthesis methods but also helps address environmental pollution caused by agricultural waste. In this study, Siamese banana peel (SBP) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for the synthesis of AgNPs. The effects of reaction time, AgNO3 solution concentration, and the volume ratio between the AgNO3 solution and banana peel extract on the formation of AgNPs were evaluated using UV-Vis spectroscopy via surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The physicochemical characteristics of AgNPs under optimal conditions were assessed via UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, and HR-TEM analyses. Antibacterial activity was evaluated by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) against nine microbial strains, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The results showed that the suitable synthesis conditions included a reaction time of 120 minutes, an AgNO3 concentration of 2.0 mM, and an AgNO3 solution-to-extract volume ratio of 30 : 20 (v/v). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis revealed that the nanoparticles were predominantly spherical, well-dispersed, with sizes ranging within 28.3 ± 10.1 nm. XRD and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) analyses indicated that the AgNPs possessed a face-centered cubic (fcc) crystalline structure of metallic silver, whereas FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of phytochemical functional groups involved in nanoparticle formation and surface stabilization. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited antibacterial activity across all tested strains, with MIC/MBC ratios ranging from 2 to 4, demonstrating significant bactericidal efficacy under the experimental conditions.

articles.titulo: Soil-plant interactions regulating the mobility and acquisition of Zn, Fe, Se, and I: implications for crop biofortification strategies
articles.autores: Zevallos S, Gutierrez-Vilchez P, … Guimarães Guilherme LR (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Micronutrient deficiencies, particularly those involving zinc (Zn), iron (Fe), selenium (Se), and iodine (I), remain major constraints to human nutrition and food security. Crop biofortification offers a sustainable approach to increasing the concentration and bioavailability of these elements in staple foods. Still, its effectiveness depends on the processes regulating their behavior across the soil-plantsoil-plant continuum. This structured narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the edaphic, rhizospheric, physiological, and molecular mechanisms controlling Zn, Fe, Se, and I mobility, acquisition, transport, redistribution, storage, and accumulation in edible plant organs. Literature searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar, focusing primarily on studies published between 2021 and 18 March 2026, while retaining foundational research required to explain key mechanisms. The evidence indicates that parent material, texture, cation exchange capacity, pH, redox potential, organic matter, and nutrient interactions govern micronutrient speciation and availability. Plants respond through rhizosphere acidification, chelator and organic acid release, microbial associations, and coordinated transporter networks. Zinc and Fe homeostasis involves ZIP/IRT, HMA, YSL, NRAMP, MTP, VIT, and related transport systems. In contrast, Se largely shares sulfate and phosphate pathways, and iodine appears to use anion transport systems associated with chloride. Agronomic fertilization can rapidly increase micronutrient concentrations, while breeding, biotechnology, and gene editing can improve uptake, remobilization, and storage. The most promising strategies integrate soil diagnosis, appropriate nutrient sources and application methods, genotype selection, microbial processes, bioavailability, and food-system considerations. Such integration is essential for producing nutritionally improved crops without compromising yield, environmental sustainability, or consumer acceptance.

articles.titulo: Indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1-targeted redox remodeling by a mesoporous medium-entropy alloy nanozyme promotes ferroptosis and cuproptosis for tumor therapy
articles.autores: Wang C, Chen C, … Lan J (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tumor cells exhibit robust redox adaptive capacity, limiting the effectiveness of ROS amplification alone in inducing persistent and irreversible oxidative damage. Accordingly, simultaneously enhancing oxidative stress and disrupting antioxidant defenses represents an effective strategy for improving catalytic cancer therapy. Here, we developed hyaluronic acid-functionalized NLG-919-loaded mesoporous PtPdRhCu medium-entropy alloy colloidal nanoparticles (PPRCNH), an interface-engineered platform integrating porous architecture, multimetallic electronic coupling, surface functionalization, and metabolic regulation. The mesoporous framework exposes abundant low-coordination catalytic sites, while interactions among Pt, Pd, Rh, and Cu promote H2O2 activation and sustained ROS production. HA functionalization facilitates the uptake of PPRCNH by CD44-overexpressing osteosarcoma cells, whereas NLG-919 inhibits indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1)-dependent tryptophan-to-kynurenine conversion, consequently impairing G6PD-mediated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) regeneration. The acidic tumor microenvironment further accelerates Cu release and perturbs mitochondrial lipoylated protein homeostasis. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that PPRCNH enhanced ROS generation and suppressed antioxidant compensation dependent on glutathione (GSH) and NADPH, resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction and the simultaneous induction of ferroptosis and cuproptosis. In the osteosarcoma model, PPRCNH achieved a tumor growth inhibition rate of approximately 77.2%. This study establishes a catalytic-metabolic regulatory paradigm by integrating mesoporous medium-entropy alloy interfaces with metabolic checkpoint modulation to achieve sustained oxidative stress amplification.

articles.titulo: New mechanistic insights into aeration-driven utilization of extracellular organic matter as carbon reservoir for simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus removal in mainstream partial nitritation/anammox
articles.autores: Choi S, Chun M, … Choi D (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aeration strategy-driven utilization of extracellular organic matter was investigated as a key mechanism regulating simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus removal in a mainstream partial nitritation/anammox (PN/A) system. The metabolic pathways through which functional microbial groups utilized organic matter at different C/N ratios depended on the aeration strategy. At high C/N ratios, intermittent aeration promoted aerobic utilization of organic matter, contributing to more rapid suppression of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) and favoring anammox activity. In contrast, at low C/N ratios, Single-stage aeration favored organic matter retention in loosely bound extracellular polymeric substances (LB-EPS), which served as a potential extracellular carbon reservoir. During the anoxic phase, this carbon supported partial denitrification and denitrifying polyphosphate-accumulating organisms, contributing to simultaneous anammox-based nitrogen removal and phosphorus removal. During the aerobic phase, its utilization intensified heterotrophic competition for O2, contributing to NOB suppression. This coordinated utilization supported stable total nitrogen and phosphorus removal efficiencies of 88.5 ± 4.3 % and 73.3 ± 2.4 %, respectively, at a C/N ratio of 2. Microbial community analysis further revealed greater network modularity and more positive associations under Single-stage aeration, whereas intermittent aeration was associated with greater NOB dominance and community variability. Overall, aeration strategy was associated with extracellular carbon utilization by aerobic and anoxic microbial communities, shaping the pathways involved in simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus removal. These findings provide mechanistic insights into aeration control in mainstream PN/A, extending its role beyond NOB suppression to the regulation of extracellular carbon utilization.

articles.titulo: Optimizing bacterial enrichment procedures to improve mosquito midgut microbiome research
articles.autores: Schrieke H, Trouche B, … Reveillaud J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquitoes are major vectors of infectious diseases, with their midgut microbiota playing a crucial role in host development, reproduction, and pathogen interactions. However, characterizing midgut microbial communities remains challenging because host DNA often dominates metagenomic libraries, reducing the resolution of bacterial community profiling and hindering the recovery of microbial genomes. To evaluate strategies for bacterial DNA enrichment in this context, we compared three DNA extraction protocols applied to pooled Aedes aegypti midguts: (i) the QIAGEN DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit without filtration (DNeasy NF), (ii) the same kit preceded by a 5 μm filtration step to reduce eukaryotic material (DNeasy F), and (iii) the QIAGEN QIAamp Microbiome kit, which combines differential host cell lysis and enzymatic DNA depletion. Each method was assessed using qPCR-based quantification of bacterial and host DNA, SSU rRNA-based taxonomic profiling of metagenomic reads, and Metagenome-Assembled Genomes (MAGs) reconstruction using advanced binning approaches. Our results show that while the Microbiome kit provided the highest bacterial enrichment and captured a large fraction (> 85%) of the bacterial taxa detected with the other kits, it yielded a higher relative abundance of Gammaproteobacteria. This occurred without a loss of overall diversity, suggesting improved recovery of microbial taxa rather than a compositional bias. The filtration step associated with the DNeasy kit significantly reduced host DNA but also lowered bacterial material, allowing MAG reconstruction, though less efficiently than the Microbiome kit. Despite this, the DNeasy methods allowed recovering a broader range of bacterial phyla with a more even distribution across taxa, while each extraction method also detected a unique set of NTUs. Overall, a combination of DNA extraction methods may be necessary to optimize microbiome analysis in mosquito midguts, facilitating a more comprehensive understanding of microbial diversity and its potential applications in vector control strategies.

articles.titulo: Mosquito vector abundance, spatial distribution and arboviral transmission risk in high-traffic cross-border zones of Tanzania
articles.autores: Kakulu R, Kemibala E, … Kimaro EG (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Arboviral diseases remain a major global public health challenge because mosquito vectors continue to expand their geographical range through increasing international travel, urbanization and climate change. This study aimed to assess the abundance, spatial distribution and larval indices of mosquito vectors of medical importance in a cross-border setting. A comprehensive entomological survey, using multiple collection techniques, was conducted between October and November 2024 at high-traffic cross-border zones at Mutukula ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Uganda and Namanga ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Kenya. Adult mosquitoes were collected using BG-Pro traps, CDC light traps and Prokopack aspirators, while larval surveys were conducted through cross-sectional household inspections of potential breeding habitats. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, and associations between variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Binomial and Poisson regression models were used to identify factors associated with mosquito abundance and breeding site occurrence, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 6952 mosquitoes were collected, comprising Culex quinquefasciatus (84.7%, n = 5895), Aedes aegypti (10.0%, n = 689) and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (5.3%, n = 369). Significantly higher abundance of Aedes spp. and Anopheles funestus s.l was recorded in hamlets located within 400 m of the international border (p < 0.0001), whereas Culex quinquefasciatus predominated in hamlets situated beyond 400 m from the border (χ2 = 1938, p < 0.000001). One female Aedes albopictus was detected among the adult Aedes collections, suggesting the potential introduction of this invasive vector. Four of the 10 hamlets surveyed had larval indices exceeding recommended thresholds, indicating an elevated risk of arboviral transmission. This study revealed a high prevalence of Aedes aegypti within the cross-border buffer zone and a broader distribution of Culex species beyond this zone. These findings underscore the urgent need for sustained vector control interventions and strengthened entomological surveillance and control beyond the International Health Regulations (2005) as amended in 2024, which recommended a 400 m buffer zone at points of entry to mitigate the risk of arboviral disease transmission and potential epidemics.

articles.titulo: Role of Anopheles funestus in sustaining residual malaria transmission in central Senegal
articles.autores: Faye MB, Dia AK, … Samb B (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Anopheles funestus is one of the major malaria vectors in sub-Saharan Africa. In Senegal, it is found across nearly all biogeographical areas, often replacing An. gambiae s.l. and sustaining malaria transmission during the dry season. Despite its recognized role as a major vector, the specific contribution of An. funestus to malaria transmission in many malaria-endemic areas remains underexplored. This study aims to assess the contribution of An. funestus in malaria transmission in two health districts in Central Senegal.
Adult mosquitoes were collected from July 2018 to November 2019 in the health districts of Nioro (Ndramé Ndimb) and Ndoffane (Tawa Mboudaye) using Human Landing Catches (HLCs) and Pyrethrum Spray Catches (PSCs). Anopheline specimens were identified morphologically using standard dichotomous keys, with species confirmation performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Plasmodium falciparum infection and blood meals sources were determined using Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) techniques.
A total of 6,932 Anopheles mosquitoes were collected. Of these, 73.7% (5,108/6,932) were identified as An. funestus, which was the predominant species at both study sites, with 1,364 specimens collected in Nioro and 3,744 in Ndoffane. Molecular analysis confirmed that An. funestus sensu stricto (s.s) was the only member of the An. funestus group recorded. In Ndramé Ndimb, the mean human biting rate and indoor resting density were 2.8 bites per person per night (b/p/n) and 9.0 females per room (f/r), respectively, compared to 12.4 b/p/n and 19.1 f/r in Tawa Mboudaye. The P. falciparum circumsporozoite rate was 0.3% in both villages, resulting in estimated entomological inoculation rates (EIRs) of 0.008 and 0.038 infected bites per person per night in Ndramé Ndimb and Tawa Mboudaye, respectively. The human blood index was relatively low, with only 22.3% (324/1,452) of An. funestus specimens found to have fed on humans.
This study highlights the predominance of An. funestus and its important role in sustaining residual malaria transmission in central Senegal, even where overall transmission intensity remains low.

v6.implicacao: Medida de índice de sangue humano por ELISA: referência para o tema fonte-repasto da Xenovigilância (Rio + portos).
v6.resumo: Em dois distritos do centro do Senegal (2018–2019), An. funestus s.s. foi 73,7% de 6.932 Anopheles; taxa de circunsporozoíto de 0,3% e EIR de 0,008 e 0,038 picadas infectantes por pessoa por noite; só 22,3% de 1.452 fêmeas alimentadas tinham sangue humano.
v6.metodo: Capturas em isca humana e spray de piretro, identificação morfológica com confirmação por PCR, ELISA para P. falciparum e para fonte do sangue.

articles.titulo: Individual variation in food odor sensitivity is related to neuropeptide signaling and starvation in
articles.autores: Okumura M, Shibukawa Y, … Chihara T (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Olfaction is fundamental for animal survival, and individual variation exists in olfactory sensitivity. However, the underlying mechanisms of such variations remain unclear. We classified Drosophila with different olfactory sensitivities toward food-related odors from the same genetic stock using sequential olfactory trap assays. Transcriptome analysis of sensitive and insensitive flies, defined by consistent attraction or non-attraction across three assays, revealed differential expression of genes associated with chemosensation, lipid metabolism, and lipid transport. Flies attracted to food-related odors exhibited lower triacylglycerol levels than non-attracted flies. Sensitive flies also expressed higher levels of sNPF-R, a neuropeptide receptor induced by starvation, despite all flies being exposed to the same starvation stress before the trap assays. Moreover, sensitive flies were more vulnerable to starvation, and feeding decreased their attraction to food-related odors. Together, these findings indicate that individual variation in internal physiological state, particularly starvation level, influences olfactory sensitivity to food-related odors through neuropeptide signaling.

v6.implicacao: Para SNC de mosquitos (neuropeptídeos) e Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes: desenho transferível para correlacionar estado nutricional individual (TAG) com busca por hospedeiro em Ae. aegypti após repastos distintos; hipótese a testar.
v6.resumo: Em Drosophila de um mesmo estoque, a sensibilidade a odores de alimento varia entre indivíduos: as sensíveis têm menos triacilglicerol, são mais vulneráveis à inanição e expressam mais um receptor de neuropeptídeo induzido por inanição; alimentar reduz a atração. O transcriptoma aponta genes de quimiossensação e de metabolismo e transporte de lipídios.
